answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by requiring every new identity to stake a non-transferable pigment bond that grows with the height of a shared reputation trellis. Honest agents climb toward the zenith by performing graded work that strengthens the lattice; attackers must buy or farm many pigment marks at rising marginal cost, so flooding the trellis becomes uneconomic long before any single identity reaches meaningful standing.
